note: Settled facts about Design Bees, stated by AJ. Every teammate sees these before doing anything. If something here is wrong, AJ corrects it once and it is corrected for the whole hive — nobody should ever ask about these again.

facts.fact: In BILLING DATA (Wix transactions, snapshots, cohorts), 'Honeycomb' and 'Honeycomb Plus' are the SAME plan — treat them as one everywhere, never report them as two, never count a move between them as an upgrade. In CUSTOMER-FACING COPY the canonical names are exactly: Worker Bee, Buzz Basics, Honey Comb (two words), Nectar Pro. There are FOUR plans, never 'three plans', and 'Honeycomb Plus' or 'Nectar' alone never appear in copy.

Worker Bee $545/mo (16 hrs, ~$34/hr), Buzz Basics $995/mo (30 hrs, ~$33/hr), Honey Comb $1,645/mo (53 hrs, ~$31/hr), Nectar Pro $2,645/mo (74 hrs, ~$36/hr). AUD inc GST. The old 20/33/55/88 hours ladder is RETIRED — any copy or draft quoting it is wrong. Anything under $100 is not a plan payment.

Richard Lowe converted on Buzz Basics. Design Bees completed his logo and branding within 48 hours. He stayed a few months, then cancelled the subscription because he ran out of design work — NOT because of dissatisfaction, price or a competitor. He is still a customer: he now sends a brief for one-off jobs when he needs them, charged at an hourly rate for custom work. Do not describe this as churn or a loss, and do not ask AJ about it again — he has explained it three times.

Peter Nittes was deliberately signed for a ~3 month engagement so Design Bees could deliver a full new suite of logos. That was the intent from the start. The later call was AJ trying to extend him into an ongoing client, not a churn conversation. Do not record this as a lost client or a budget objection.

Design Bees is a design subscription agency: unlimited graphic design on a monthly plan, human designers only. Clients running out of design work is a normal and expected reason to pause or cancel, not a failure of the service.

No LinkedIn post or blog post is written until there is verified search demand or clear buyer intent behind it — a Tom-assessed gap, a Ricky-evidenced pain, or an item AJ curated into the blog engine content queue. Volume is not the goal. The blog engine operator pack (in the repo at server/data/blog-engine/) is the authoritative content standard; its non-negotiables and five gates apply to everything.

A direct customer quote may only be used in content if it genuinely adds value, is not revealing or negative, AND AJ has approved that specific use beforehand. The same approval applies to using a real client — or a thinly-veiled version of one, e.g. 'a furniture company' when we have exactly one furniture client — as a hypothetical or worked example. Raise the proposal with AJ first; draft without it while waiting. Generic hypotheticals that map to no real client are fine.

GA4 and Search Console are wired read-only via Google OAuth, live only once AJ consents to the new scopes at /auth/google. An impression, click, session or position number may be stated ONLY when an analytics tool returned it this run, cited as GA4 or GSC. Ahrefs and all keyword-volume tools remain unconnected — nobody ever states a search volume or difficulty. Everything else stays qualitative and labelled as such.
